Orthogonal-polynomial analysis: nonnegative integrable weight function w on a real interval, of positive finite total integral and sufficient finite absolute moments.

Commutative algebra: square-zero ideal I of a commutative unital ring A, characterized by I²={0} (equivalently ab=0 for all a,b∈I). The square-zero property is strictly stronger than mere nilpotence of an unspecified positive exponent.
Abelian category theory: canonical morphism Coim(f)→Im(f) induced by factorization of f through its coimage and image, an isomorphism in an abelian category.
General topology: finite subfamily of a given open cover (U_i)_{i∈I} indexed by finite F⊆I such that ⋃_{i∈F}U_i=X; the existence of one for every cover defines compactness.
Category theory: compatible cocone from a filtered diagram (M_i) to X, comprising maps M_i→X commuting with transition arrows; X need not be their colimit.
Graph theory: adjacency relation between distinct vertices u and v of a loopless undirected graph, holding exactly when {u,v}∈E.
Elementary number theory: Euclidean division remainder r of integer a by positive modulus m, uniquely satisfying a=qm+r and 0≤r<m.
query: least nonnegative remainder upon division by m

context: Sheaf of modules over the structure sheaf O_X on a locally ringed space, with compatible restriction maps.
Euclidean vector u∈ℝ^n with Euclidean norm ∥u∥₂=1, a normalized direction.

Order theory: infimum inf(A) of a subset A of a partially ordered set, a lower bound greater than or equal to every other lower bound, when one exists; here the set consists of admissible positive real bounds and may have infimum zero.
Set theory: arbitrary intersection of a family of subsets of V, here specialized to the family of convex supersets of U; its specialization equals the convex hull.

Commutative algebra: extension of scalars of a commutative unital k-algebra A along a field extension K/k, giving K-algebra A⊗_k K with multiplication (a⊗u)(b⊗v)=ab⊗uv, unit 1⊗1, and the canonical k-algebra map A→A⊗_k K.
query: k-algebra A and its scalar-extension K-algebra

context: Module theory: canonical R-linear tensor/product comparison induced by product projections π_j:∏_iQ_i→Q_j, mapping m⊗(q_i)_i to (m⊗q_j)_j; its injectivity for every family is the Mittag-Leffler criterion.
Set theory: power set of an arbitrary underlying set X, namely the collection of all subsets of X; variable names X and S are interchangeable.
Ordered group theory: a bijective group homomorphism φ:Γ→(ℤ,+) that preserves and reflects the group order, where Γ is the value group and ℤ has its usual total order.
query: isomorphism of ordered groups with Z

context: Orthogonal-polynomial analysis: countably infinite set X of distinct real support points for a countably atomic weighted sum; the word discrete concerns the sum, not necessarily discrete topology of X.
Sheaf theory: restriction F|_U of a sheaf F of rings on X to an open subspace U, assigning F(V) to each open V in U with inherited restriction morphisms.
query: restriction of the structure sheaf O_X|_U

context: Category theory: cocone from a diagram F:I→C to vertex Q, a compatible natural transformation F⇒constant_Q with arrows F(i)→Q satisfying diagram commutativity.
query: cocone morphisms F(i)→Q compatible with the diagram

context: Category theory: contravariant Hom operation α:T'→T sends a morphism h:T→X to h∘α:T'→X and respects compositions/identity.

Probability: equality of two real random variables outside a P-null exceptional set, here conditional expectation E[X_{n+1}|F_n] and X_n for each fixed n≥0. The almost-sure equality notion is reusable; the conditional-expectation martingale identity is source-specific.

Module theory: submodule generated by a subset S of a left R-module M, consisting of all finite R-linear combinations of elements of S; for a finite S={m_1,...,m_n} this is the finite R-linear span Σ_i R m_i, possibly all of M.
query: submodule generated by the differences ι_i(m)−ι_j(μ_ij(m))

context: General set theory/topology: family (F_i) of subsets of X with ⋂_{i∈E}F_i nonempty for every nonempty finite E of indices; specify the empty-family convention separately.
Set theory: countable union ⋃_{n≥1}A_n={x:there exists positive integer n with x∈A_n} of an indexed sequence of subsets of X.

Commutative algebra: product IJ of two ideals of a commutative unital ring R, generated by finite sums of pairwise products; ordinary ideal powers I^n for n≥1 by repeated ideal multiplication, and by convention I^0=R when nonnegative exponents are used.
Probability theory: integrable real random variable X on a probability space with E[|X|]<∞, equivalently ∫|X|dP finite; applies separately to X and Z.
query: integrability of real random variable X and Z

context: Module theory: direct sum ⊕_{i∈I} M_i of a family of left R-modules M_i, each generated by at most countably many elements over R, with elements finite-support tuples and coordinatewise module operations; the index family I need not be countable.
query: direct sum of countably generated R-modules

context: Category theory: isomorphism of fibred categories over common base C, with an inverse commuting strictly with projection functors.
Set theory: relative complement X\A={x∈X:x∉A}, where A⊆X; in a sigma-algebra it is applied to each measurable member A.

Field theory: evaluation map of Galois-group automorphisms at a fixed element a∈E, ev_a:Gal(E/F)→E, σ↦σ(a), where its continuity is relative to the chosen topologies; distinct from polynomial evaluation homomorphisms.
Commutative algebra: base-change κ(p)-algebra S⊗_R κ(p) of a unital commutative R-algebra S, with multiplication (s⊗a)(t⊗b)=st⊗ab, unit 1⊗1 and κ(p)-algebra structure.
query: tensor-product algebra structure on S⊗_R κ(p)

context: Field theory: intermediate subfield L between a specified field inclusion k⊆K, satisfying k⊆L⊆K with the inherited field operations. It need not be algebraically closed or finite over k.

Commutative algebra: product IJ of two ideals of a commutative unital ring R, generated by finite sums of pairwise products; ordinary ideal powers I^n for n≥1 by repeated ideal multiplication, and by convention I^0=R when nonnegative exponents are used.
Module category: covariant functor Hom_R(P,−) from R-Mod to abelian groups/modules where appropriate, sending N to Hom_R(P,N), g:N→N' to postcomposition g∘−.
Metric geometry: distance between two subsets A,B of a metric space, defined as inf{d(a,b):a∈A,b∈B}, with an explicit convention for empty subsets.
Linear algebra: main diagonal entries a_{ii} of an n by n square matrix, with coincident row and column index.
Category theory: family of hom-set bijections Hom_D(LX,Y)≅Hom_C(X,RY), indexed by X∈C,Y∈D, with each hom class set-valued under needed local-smallness conventions.
query: bijections between the morphisms L(X) to Y in D and X to R(Y) in C

context: Quasi-coherent tilde construction M↦~M on Spec(R) whose principal-open sections identify with localizations M_f.
query: sheaf ~M associated with some R-module M

context: Order theory: order isomorphism f:(A,≤_A)→(B,≤_B), a bijection preserving and reflecting order; for well-ordered sets this identifies equal ordinal order types.

Polynomial algebra over a field: a simple root α of f in a field extension means f(α)=0 and f'(α)≠0, equivalently (x−α)^2 does not divide f over that extension field. For reduction modulo a maximal ideal the root and derivative are taken in the residue field.
query: simple zero of reduced polynomial f-bar over κ

context: Elementary number theory: prime integer p>1 with positive divisors precisely 1 and p; unlike a prime ideal in a ring.

Module theory: finite-rank free left R-module R^n over a unital ring R for finite n≥0, the direct sum of n copies of the regular left R-module, with its canonical standard basis; not the same as an arbitrary locally free module.
General topological sequence convergence: eventual containment in every neighborhood of limit, here in T^D with product topology.
Category theory: compatible cone over a cospan f:X→S, g:Y→S, consisting of arrows p:P→X,q:P→Y with fp=gq; P not necessarily a pullback.
query: commuting cone to arrows X→S and Y→S

context: Real analysis: open real interval (a,b)={x∈ℝ:a<x<b}, allowing source-specific bounded or unbounded endpoints where stated.

Von Neumann ordinals: the zero ordinal is the empty set ∅, the least ordinal under membership/order, and is excluded from the present definition of a limit ordinal even though it is not a successor ordinal.

General topology: at a fixed point x of X, a neighborhood basis consisting of connected neighborhoods, such that for every neighborhood U of x some connected neighborhood V of x satisfies V⊆U; V need not be declared open unless the chosen convention explicitly requires it.
Probability: for each ordered pair of indices 0≤n≤m, the real random variables E[X_m|F_n] and X_n agree P-almost surely; not a pointwise equality for every ω∈Ω.
Homological algebra: nonnegatively graded cochain complex (C^p,d^p) of modules with d^{p+1}∘d^p=0, together with its degree-indexed structure; this de Rham instance also carries wedge multiplication.
Module theory: for R-linear φ:M→N and multiplicative S=R∖p, induced localized map S^{-1}φ:S^{-1}M→S^{-1}N defined by m/s↦φ(m)/s; the p-localized map φ_p is R_p-linear.
query: localization of the module homomorphism φ_p:M_p→N_p

context: Commutative algebra: the ideal (f,g) of k[X] generated by two polynomials f,g is the set of all polynomial combinations af+bg with a,b∈k[X], an ideal of their common polynomial ring.
Algebra: two-sided identity element e for binary operation * on G, satisfying e*a=a*e=a for all a∈G; existence and uniqueness in a group are special consequences.

Field theory: simple generated extension F(α)⊆E, the smallest subfield of the extension field E that contains base field F and selected α∈E; its elements are rational expressions in α with coefficients in F and nonzero denominators.
query: smallest subfield containing F and alpha

context: Set theory: equivalence relation generated by prescribed ordered pairs P⊆S×S, the smallest reflexive symmetric transitive relation containing P; here S is the disjoint union of F(i) and P identifies each x with F(u)(x).
Real analysis: convergence domain D={z∈ℝ:∑_{n≥0}c_nz^n converges} of a real power series with coefficients c_n, here c_n=a_n/n!.

Module theory: submodule generated by a subset S of a left R-module M, consisting of all finite R-linear combinations of elements of S; for a finite S={m_1,...,m_n} this is the finite R-linear span Σ_i R m_i, possibly all of M.
Category theory: isomorphism in a category, a morphism f:X→Y possessing an inverse g:Y→X with gf=id_X and fg=id_Y, not just a bijection of underlying sets.
Order theory and topology: finite chain Z₀⊊Z₁⊊⋯⊊Z_n of distinct irreducible closed subsets of space X ordered by strict inclusion; chain length n counts inclusions, not the number n+1 of subsets.
query: strict finite chain of irreducible closed subsets

context: Set theory: a set α is transitive when each of its elements is a subset of α; equivalently whenever x∈y∈α then x∈α. This property is independent of the separate well-ordering requirement.
Homeomorphism from Z to its image as closed subset of X equipped with subspace topology.
Set theory: intersection ⋂_{i∈F}U_i of finitely many subsets of ambient X, including the empty-index intersection X; topology requires this intersection to lie in τ.
Commutative algebra: for a prime ideal p of a commutative ring R, the complement S=R∖p is a multiplicatively closed subset containing 1, and localization M_p means S^{-1}M for an R-module M.
Field theory: bijective unital field homomorphism, here from prime subfield to ℚ in characteristic zero or 𝔽_p in characteristic p; distinguished from mere bijection of sets.
Set theory/topology: relative complements X\U of quasi-compact open U⊆X; these need not be open in the original spectral topology.

Commutative algebra: polynomial algebra R[X_i : i in I] over a commutative unital coefficient ring R, for an arbitrary set I of independent indeterminates; each polynomial has finite monomial support. Includes the one-variable and finite-variable cases and polynomial algebras over fields and quotient coefficient rings.
General topology: restricted Cartesian product ∏_{i∈I}U_i where each U_i is open in X_i and U_i=X_i except for finitely many i.
query: basic product of open coordinate sets

context: Set theory: preimage or inverse image of subset B⊆Y under an arbitrary function f:X→Y, defined as f^{-1}[B]={x∈X:f(x)∈B}; notation f^{-1}[B] never presupposes that f is invertible. Includes underlying set preimages of open/measurable sets and contractions of prime ideals under ring homomorphisms, where additional structure is a separate condition.
query: inverse image of each quasi-compact open subset

context: Set theory: preimage or inverse image of subset B⊆Y under an arbitrary function f:X→Y, defined as f^{-1}[B]={x∈X:f(x)∈B}; notation f^{-1}[B] never presupposes that f is invertible. Includes underlying set preimages of open/measurable sets and contractions of prime ideals under ring homomorphisms, where additional structure is a separate condition.
Category theory: categorical product of a finite family of objects, with the empty product convention giving a terminal object; binary products alone are not the full finite-family construction.
query: finite categorical products including empty product

context: Commutative algebra: quotient ring A/I of a commutative unital ring A by an ideal I, with elements additive cosets a+I, operations induced from A and canonical surjective unital quotient map A→A/I. Set theory: ℵ₀, the least infinite cardinal, cardinality of the natural numbers; appears as a lower bound in the Stacks size convention.

Set theory: preimage or inverse image of subset B⊆Y under an arbitrary function f:X→Y, defined as f^{-1}[B]={x∈X:f(x)∈B}; notation f^{-1}[B] never presupposes that f is invertible. Includes underlying set preimages of open/measurable sets and contractions of prime ideals under ring homomorphisms, where additional structure is a separate condition.
Linear algebra: n×n identity matrix over a unital commutative ring, entries δ_ij equal 1_R on the diagonal and 0_R elsewhere.

Commutative algebra: quotient ring A/I of a commutative unital ring A by an ideal I, with elements additive cosets a+I, operations induced from A and canonical surjective unital quotient map A→A/I. This includes prime-ideal quotients, polynomial-ring quotients and ideal-power quotients; a quotient's being a field, local ring or R-algebra requires additional conditions.
Field theory: isomorphism φ:K→L of field extensions of k with φ∘ι_K=ι_L for the chosen embeddings of k into K,L; under identified k-subfields φ fixes every element of k.
query: isomorphic as an extension of k

context: Module theory: S-linear map of S-modules preserving S-action; required for order-zero differential operators.

Category theory: diagram as ordinary functor F:I→C, with no source-stated restriction that both indexing and target categories be small; the indexed small-category covariant functor would impose extra hypotheses.
Order theory: a subset A of a partially ordered set S is bounded above if some u∈S satisfies a≤u for all a∈A; not a numerical finite-bound assumption only.
Stalkwise homomorphisms f_x^#:O_{Y,f(x)}→O_{X,x} induced by morphism of sheaves of rings.
Complex analysis/algebra: modulus |z| of z∈ℂ, the nonnegative real sqrt((Re z)^2+(Im z)^2), used for absolute homogeneity over complex scalars.

Polynomial algebra over fields: a root (zero) α∈K of a univariate polynomial f∈F[x] in a field extension K/F means f(α)=0_K using coefficient inclusion F→K and polynomial evaluation; includes the residue class of x in K=F[x]/(f) for nonconstant f.
query: roots of a polynomial in a field

context: Algebra/order theory: bijective field homomorphism F→K whose map and inverse preserve field operations and the total order, not merely an ordered-set bijection.
Real analysis: coefficient sequence (a_n) indexed by ℕ_0 with values in ℝ, without assuming convergence of the sequence or its generating power series.
Category theory: ordinary covariant functor F:I→C from a small indexing category I to an arbitrary locally small target category C; no smallness requirement on C.
query: diagram as functor from indexing category

context: Commutative algebra: kernel ideal of a unital homomorphism φ:A→B of commutative rings, consisting of all a∈A mapped to 0_B; for a polynomial evaluation map it is the ideal of polynomial relations, and for a quotient-localization composite it is the inverse image of zero in the target ring.
Real topology: deleted δ-neighborhood {x∈ℝ:0<|x−a|<δ} of a, intersected with the function domain; the center a itself is excluded.
Group theory: conjugate of subset N⊆G by g∈G, the subset {gng^{-1}:n∈N} obtained by conjugating every element.
Set theory: arbitrary indexed intersection ⋂_{F∈𝔽}F of subsets of X, here 𝔽 comprises the closed F containing A; identifying this intersection with cl_X(A) is the definition of closure.
query: intersection of all closed supersets of A

context: Commutative algebra: R-subalgebra of unital R-algebra S generated by a finite family s_1,…,s_n, the smallest unital R-subalgebra containing their elements, equal to the image of evaluation R[X_1,…,X_n]→S; its being all of S is the finite-type condition.
query: R-algebra generated by finitely many elements

context: Category theory: ordinary category with objects, morphisms, identities and associative composition, without requiring its collection of objects to be a set; any size assumptions are stated separately.
Commutative algebra: scalar extension of commutative unital k-algebra A to field extension K/k, the commutative K-algebra A⊗_k K with multiplication (a⊗x)(b⊗y)=ab⊗xy.
Set theory: inverse image f^{-1}(B)={x∈X:f(x)∈B} of a subset B⊆Y under f:X→Y; here B={0_W}.

Commutative algebra: for a unital homomorphism f:R→S of commutative rings, the induced canonical R-algebra multiplication map μ:S⊗_R S→S, μ(s⊗t)=st; its being an isomorphism is the ring-epimorphism criterion.
query: multiplication map S⊗_R S→S is ring isomorphism

context: Category theory: natural transformation α:G⇒H between functors over a base C, with components α_s:G(s)→H(s) commuting with source-category arrows and with projection to identity arrows in C.
Monoidal category theory: coevaluation η:1→X⊗Y and evaluation ε:Y⊗X→1 forming unit/counit data for a left dual pair Y of X.

General topology: an open neighborhood U of a specified point x∈X, meaning x∈U and U belongs to the topology of X; local Krull dimension here ranges over all such U with their induced subspace topologies.
